//: Which Slack channel a follow-up case should be opened in.
Every channel named here must exist in the workspace AND have the bot
invited to it. A channel the bot is not in fails at post time with
`channel_not_found`, which reads as though the channel is missing rather
than as though the bot is not a member.
Rules are tried in this order and the first match wins:
1. parties  — matched against the work order's `assigned_to` text. This is
the strongest signal because a supervisor has already named
who does the work. Aliases match whole words only.
2. zones    — matched geographically, by which zone centroid the drain
sits nearest. Empty here: no zone channels exist yet.
3. default  — everything else.
`default_channel` is empty on purpose. With only two channels most
follow-ups match neither, and the honest answer is that this one is not
going to Slack at all — the console says so, and the work order is still
recorded. The alternative is proposing a channel that does not exist and
discovering it only when the post fails.
Add a catch-all by creating the channel, inviting the bot, and naming it
here. Same for `escalation_channel`, which is offered alongside the primary
route for anything at or above `escalate_above_severity`.
